body.en: Your uncle says: 'It rained hard yesterday, so this climate change talk isn't real — the weather is just doing what weather does.' What's the best response?

choices.label: One rainy day is weather. Decades of rainfall becoming heavier and less predictable is climate.
choices.consequence: Exactly right. Weather is what's happening right now; climate is the long-term pattern behind it. A single storm doesn't prove or disprove climate change — the trend over years does.

choices.label: Agree with him — one normal-looking rainy day means the climate is fine.
choices.consequence: Not quite. A single day of rain, on its own, tells you nothing about the climate — it's the long-term pattern of heavier, less predictable rain that's the real signal.

choices.label: Tell him climate change means it should basically never rain normally again.
choices.consequence: That overstates it. Climate change shifts patterns and intensity over time — it doesn't mean every single day becomes abnormal.
